title: The Afternoon Brief: Bitcoin Holds Near $77,200 as Onto-Exchange Flow Persists
dek: The desk's boards show bitcoin up 0.2% on the day and 21.79% over the past week to $77,234.25, even as whale flows have moved onto exchanges since the week ending Aug 16, now $1,062 million for the week ending Aug 23.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: ETF inflows and rising weekly prices continue alongside a whale flow pattern that has favored exchanges since the week ending Aug 16, a split the reporting does not explain.
bottom_line: Bitcoin held near $77,234.25 on the desk's boards, up 0.2% on the day and 21.79% over the past week, while Pakistan announced the end of its near decade-long crypto ban through a new Virtual Assets Act framework whose licensing and enforcement details remain unreported. The desk's ETF flows board shows both bitcoin and ether funds posting a fifth consecutive day of net inflows through 21 Aug 2026, even as the Whale Watch board shows bitcoin and other assets moving onto exchanges, a pattern that began by the week ending Aug 16 and continued at $1,062 million for the week ending Aug 23. That divergence between fund inflows and on-chain exchange flows is not explained in the day's reporting. Coming days will test whether Pakistan's regulatory specifics emerge and whether the onto-exchange flow pattern persists against continued ETF demand.
body: Bitcoin trades near $77,234.25 on the desk's boards as of Aug 23, up 0.2% over the past 24 hours and up 21.79% over the past week and 21.07% over the past 30 days. The core split from this morning holds: fund demand and on-chain positioning are still telling different stories, and little has changed to resolve it since the morning edition.

The day's single verified story is Pakistan's end of its near decade-long cryptocurrency ban. Bilal Bin Saqib, special assistant to the prime minister on blockchain and cryptocurrency, announced the shift in an X post on Friday, per Bitcoin Magazine's reporting, introducing a framework called the Virtual Assets Act and inviting foreign businesses to build in the country. The reporting does not detail the compliance requirements, licensing structure, tax treatment, or enforcement mechanisms that will govern the new regime, so the practical shape of the policy remains unreported.

On the market side, the desk's ETF flows board shows bitcoin funds posting a net inflow of $307.5 million on 21 Aug 2026, the latest session in a run of five consecutive positive days totaling $1,917.8 million, with cumulative flows of $53,775.0 million. Ether funds added $184.0 million net on the same 21 Aug 2026 date, also a fifth straight positive day, totaling $692.6 million over that span with $12,154.0 million cumulative. Those fund-level numbers sit alongside the desk's Whale Watch board, which shows a different pattern in on-chain flows: over the past 48 hours, $180,191,848 has moved onto exchanges on a net basis across tracked assets, with bitcoin alone accounting for $205,576,013 moving onto exchanges. Ether tells the opposite story at the coin level, with $50,264,165 moving off exchanges in that same window. The board also shows $19,992,000 in stablecoin buying power, a separate metric the board does not tie causally to the exchange flows.

The weekly view on the Whale Watch board shows this onto-exchange pattern is not new. The week ending Aug 02 saw $1,075 million move off exchanges, and the week ending Aug 09 saw a further $1 million move off exchanges, but the pattern flipped by the week ending Aug 16, when $441 million moved onto exchanges, and has continued into the week ending Aug 23, when $1,062 million moved onto exchanges. That is a single week's figure, not a cumulative sum since Aug 16.

The reporting does not explain why ETF demand and on-chain exchange flows are diverging this week. The Pakistan story does not speak to market flows at all; it is a policy development running on its own track. The desk's Market Pulse shows Fear & Greed at 66, in the Greed range, with the 30-day range spanning 25 to 72, alongside elevated RSI readings across major assets including bitcoin at 80.2, ether at 78.3, and XRP at 86.5, all above 70.

The tape overall shows a market that is up sharply on the week (bitcoin's 21.79% seven-day gain, ether's 29.49%, XRP's 49.56%) while total market capitalization is down 3.03% over the past 24 hours per the desk's market board, at $2,613,302,247,800 with bitcoin dominance at 59.1%. Leverage data shows long-short ratios skewed long across the board, from BTC's 1.16 to DOGE's 3.05, with liquidations concentrated on longs in bitcoin ($11,560,725 over 20 hours) while ether shows the opposite, with short liquidations of $12,209,657 over 12 hours outpacing long liquidations of $5,166,957.

No dated regulatory checkpoints from the desk's coverage fall in the immediate days ahead; the CLARITY Act and GENIUS Act storylines carry dates already passed or set for January 2027, and the EU's MiCA and Basel threads have no stated dates in the desk's own reporting.

sources.title: Pakistan Ends Crypto Ban, Launches Virtual Assets Act Framework
